I am thinking about the mechanics of this game. Let me know if it's good or not.

This game will be a simulation of the hunger games. Each person will be randomly generated unless you want to customize. Each enemy will have a type of person which will determine how they will interact with you, friendly, evil, goal-oriented, coward, sadist, or neutral. The goal of the game is to win. Depending on your actions, if the judges think a npc or the player are worth it, they will send resources. Depending on the difficulty level, the judges might not like a person and want them to have a hard time.

To give the random generation of tributes a little bit more finesse (you never want true random - weighted random is the way to go), it'd be a good idea to randomly generate a small populace and cherry pick the two best candidates from that randomly generated populace (and yes, the ages can go from effectively "0" to - and beyond - 100).

If you really wanted to simulate the Hunger Games, you'd also want to stack the odds in certain district's favors. Certain districts would be more likely to produce NPCs with low resourcefullness but high everything else, while others would generally do better with one specific stat or environment.

Is this meant to be a multiplayer game or single player? Because Minecraft has pretty much solidified it's Hunger Games simulation. After that game type was created other games like Rust, H1Z1, Ark, and many others have been doing the same game types within their games.

The total conversion mod for Ark: Survival Evolved titled "Survival of the Fittest" already does the hunger games thing. Resource drops however are randomized because the moment you introduce "judges" you introduce bias and you screw up the game.

Players are dropped in a ring, with a bunch of resources. Grab what you can and run for the treeline. The objective is to be the last team standing. Death removes you from the remainder of the match. As time goes on, the map shrinks to ensure confrontation. When players die a big billboard in the sky lets you know. Random environmental events and day/night cycles occur during the match.
